headline: Slovakia's transport minister says his country will soon let Tesla's Full Self-Driving system be used on its roads.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the minister's statement was on 7 Oct and approval is still pending, though it is a real step in a running story.
importance_line: Tesla owners in Slovakia could soon use the system without waiting for Brussels, and each national approval strengthens Tesla's case in the EU vote; it is a minister's statement rather than a completed approval, and France, Germany, Italy and Spain have not yet approved it.
source: Drive Tesla Canada, citing Slovakia's transport minister
summary: Drive Tesla Canada reports, citing a video posted by Transport Minister Jozef Ráž on 7 Oct 2026, that Slovakia will formally recognise the Netherlands' provisional approval of the system, which still needs the driver to supervise, and so become the ninth EU country to allow it. This follows the Reuters report in our 7 Oct 2026 scan that Tesla had pressed EU officials hard to approve the software; what is new is a named country saying approval is days away, while a bloc-wide vote has slipped to December at the earliest.
notes: Read Drive Tesla Canada because the Reuters page (HTTP 401) cannot be opened; Reuters ran the story as 'Slovakia to approve Tesla's self-driving tech' on 8 Oct. Related to C11-12.
